taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Customer-approved support capabilities bound to privileged backend operations
controls.source_trace: Follow operator-selected customer identifiers to privileged reads/writes. Identify per-customer/product/action limits and whether a general support role silently bypasses them.
controls.implementation_branch: Distinguish read-only investigation, customer-approved changes and emergency roles. A backend service credential may be legitimate, provided each operation checks the support operator policy. Customer selection through a URL or search result must not silently become authority to reset factors, export private data or alter payments.
controls.operational_method: Inspect one concrete customer-approved support capability from issuance to backend use: operator, customer, purpose/action, resource version and expiry. Compare the approval tuple with the actual privileged service operation rather than merely recording a ticket number. Reusing an export approval to reset MFA or changing customer after approval is a different grant. A legitimate emergency role must be evaluated under its documented override contract, not an invented universal customer-consent rule.
controls.controlled_verification: Use a synthetic customer approval bound to one operator/action/version, then change customer, purpose or operation before an inert backend consumer. Compare actual allowed operation with rejected mismatches under any declared emergency override.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Privileged service credentials behind the console do not prove a user bypass unless the console delegates them beyond its operator policy.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Enforce operator/customer/action authorization before service calls and verify legitimate support workflows remain usable.
